body: https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/issues/24974 might also be related to this.

@rubensa can you share a sample application with a corresponding test that behaves as you describe?

That would be super useful in pinpointing the exact version in which the change started to manifest.

[Here](https://github.com/rubensa/quarkus-resteasy-reactive-bug) I prepared a sample project.

You can use it via **[VSCode](https://code.visualstudio.com/)** with the **[Remote Development](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/remote/remote-overview)** extension pack and **[Docker](https://www.docker.com/)**, via **[GitHub Codespaces](https://docs.github.com/en/codespaces)** or locally if you have **GraalVM** installed (in the provided **Docker** container for **VSCode** and **Codespaces**, **Mandrel** 23.0 for **Java** 17 is used).

As you can see in the [README](https://github.com/rubensa/quarkus-resteasy-reactive-bug/blob/main/README.md):

> The code is configured to use Quarkus 3.4.1 version with quarkus-resteasy-reactive.
> 
> I you run the provided test it (running `./mvnw test`) it will fail.
> 
> You can check that it works if you replace `quarkus.platform.version` from `3.4.1` to `3.1.3.Final` in pom.xml.
> 
> It will also work if you keep `quarkus.platform.version` as `3.4.1` but use the non-reactive **quarkus-resteasy** by replacing `quarkus-resteasy-reactive` with `quarkus-resteasy` and `quarkus-resteasy-reactive-jackson` with `quarkus-resteasy-jackson` in pom.xml.
> 


Setting up the sample project I just realized that it does not only "URL encodes" the **PathParam** but the match for the `key` in the `@Path` is not correctly resolved.

In the sample above, If you request `/base/quarkus.test.sample/objects/data/test.txt/func`, `name` is correctly resolved to `quarkus.test.sample` but `key`is incorrectly resolved to `base%2Ftest.txt/func/base/quarkus.test.sample/objects/data%2Ftest.txt` (where it should have been resolved to `data/test.txt` or `base%2Ftest.txt` if you assume the encoding problem).


Just let me know if you need anything else.

Thanks a lot.

issue.title: RealmAdminResource.getGroupByPathGroup does not work with space in path parameter

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes a PR related to a bug

labels.name: priority/important
labels.description: Must be worked on very soon

repository.name: keycloak
repository.description: Open Source Identity and Access Management For Modern Applications and Services

issue.body:
### Before reporting an issue

- [X] I have read and understood the above terms for submitting issues, and I understand that my issue may be closed without action if I do not follow them.

### Area

admin/api

### Describe the bug

I just found a regression in org.keycloak.services.resources.admin.RealmAdminResource#getGroupByPathGroup.
Path parameter values that contain a space are not decoded properly. Instead of "My Group" a group name like "My%20Group" is used for a search by name which obviously yields no results.

### Version

23.0.0

### Expected behavior

Search for a group by group path with spaces should work.

### Actual behavior

Search for a group by group path with spaces always yields not found.

### How to Reproduce?

1) Create a realm 
2) Create top level group with spaces in group name, e.g. "My Group"
3) try to search for group by path

See: `bin/kcadm.sh get realms/realmWithGroups/group-by-path/My%20Group`

### Anything else?

This is a regression and worked in Keycloak 22.0.5.

body: We are affected by this one also in keycloak (issue https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/25111). I think the reason is this PR: https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/pull/34809. In case the regex is custom (like `.*` in this case), the path param is not decoded and returned with the percent encoded characters. One workaround is using `PathSegment` which is re-encoded again.

I have not yet looked at it unfortunately. 

@rmartinc if you have a general fix in mind, by all means open a PR :)
